$comment: Bilingual menu content. `name`, `description`, `unit` and wine/variant fields are locale-keyed the same way team.json is — i18n keys (menu.category.<id>.* / menu.item.<id>.*) are derived from this file in src/lib/i18n.ts, so a new item needs no entry in el.json or en.json. `el` is the client's menu as printed and is the source of truth; `en` is a translation of it, never a different dish. A unit the client had written as a dual literal before the site was bilingual (e.g. '6 τεμάχια | 6 pieces') is split across locales like any other field — el: '6 τεμάχια', en: '6 pieces' — not carried over as one string in both. `volume` fields (ml, lt) are locale-independent and stay plain strings. price:null = not yet priced by the client; it renders as an em dash.
